narration: Welcome to the Arms & Armour gallery, where we have the personal sword of Tipu Sultan, the famed ruler of Mysore. This blade, dating from 1799 CE, is a striking example of Mysorean craftsmanship, forged from metal and finished with a wooden sheath wrapped in maroon velvet. Its hilt, a Delhishahi style, features a circular disc pommel, oval grip, and short quillons, all damascened in gold with intricate floral and creeper patterns. Along the blade itself, you’ll see gold‑etched Quranic verses, Tipu’s name, and the capital Srirangapatna, a testament to his devotion and pride. This sword, now part of the National Museum’s collection under accession number 56.17/1, survived the fall of Srirangapatna and has been preserved for us to share its history with you.
